title: Revolt of 1857
event: The Revolt of 1857 breaks out, shaking the foundations of British rule in India.

title: Calcutta, Madras & Bombay Universities Founded
event: Establishment of three premier universities at Calcutta, Madras, and Bombay.

title: Licensing Act, 1857
event: The Licensing Act of 1857 is passed to impose emergency licensing restrictions on the press.

title: Government of India Act, 1858
event: The Act for Better Government of India (1858) is passed, transferring administration from the East India Company to the British Crown.

title: Queen's Proclamation, 1858
event: The Queen's Proclamation is announced, altering the imperial administrative structure and promising non-annexation of princely states.

title: Trial of Bahadur Shah Zafar
event: Trial of the last Mughal Emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, in the Red Fort.

title: Indigo Revolt
event: Outbreak of the Indigo Revolt in Bengal, led by Digambar and Bishnu Biswas against oppressive indigo planters.

title: Civil Procedure Code Drafted
event: The Civil Procedure Code is prepared by the Law Commission.

title: The 'White Mutiny'
event: The 'White Mutiny' breaks out as European troops under the Company resent transfer of their allegiance to the Crown.

title: Indian Penal Code Compiled
event: The Indian Penal Code is compiled by the Law Commission.

title: Indian Councils Act, 1861
event: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 is enacted to introduce representative elements in the legislatures.

title: Indian Civil Service Act, 1861
event: The Indian Civil Service Act of 1861 is passed to regulate the civil services.

title: Criminal Procedure Code Compiled
event: The Criminal Procedure Code is compiled by the Law Commission.

title: Indian Police Act, 1861
event: The Indian Police Act of 1861 is enacted, creating a formal imperialist police structure.

title: Indian Mirror & Bengalee Launched
event: The first Indian daily paper in English, Indian Mirror, and the vernacular paper Bengalee are launched.

title: First Indian to Qualify ICS
event: Satyendra Nath Tagore becomes the first Indian to qualify for the Indian Civil Service (ICS).

title: Calcutta, Bombay & Madras High Courts Formed
event: The Supreme Court and the Sadar Adalats are merged into three High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.

title: Bhutan War
event: The Bhutan War takes place between the British Indian Government and Bhutan.

title: Brahmo Samaj Splits
event: A split in the Brahmo Samaj results in the creation of the Brahmo Samaj of India (led by Keshab Chandra Sen) and the Adi Brahmo Samaj (led by Debendranath Tagore).

title: Deoband School Founded
event: The Deoband School of Islamic Theology is established in Saharanpur, UP.

title: Registration Act, 1867
event: The Registration Act of 1867 replaces Metcalfe's Press Act of 1835 as a regulatory measure.

title: Prarthana Samaj Founded
event: The Prarthana Samaj is founded in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang and Govind Ranade.

title: Madras Mail Launched
event: The Madras Mail is established as the first evening newspaper in India.

title: Birth of Mahatma Gandhi
event: Birth of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi in Porbandar, Gujarat (October 2).

title: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha Founded
event: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha is founded to act as a bridge between the government and the people.

title: Indian Reform Association Founded
event: The Indian Reform Association is founded in Calcutta by Keshab Chandra Sen to promote social reform.

title: Satyashodhak Samaj Founded
event: Jyotirao Phule founds the Satyashodhak Samaj in Maharashtra to campaign against Brahminical supremacy.

title: Pabna Agrarian Uprising
event: The Pabna Agrarian Uprising breaks out in East Bengal as peasants form leagues to resist oppressive zamindars.

title: Indian League Founded
event: The Indian League is founded to stimulate nationalist feelings and political education.

title: Arya Samaj Founded
event: The Arya Samaj is founded in Bombay by Swami Dayanand Saraswati, championing Vedic revivalism.

title: Aligarh School Founded
event: The Aligarh School is founded by Syed Ahmed Khan, which later grows into the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College.

title: Theosophical Society Founded
event: The Theosophical Society is founded in New York, later shifting its headquarters to Adyar, Madras.

title: Deccan Peasants' Uprising
event: The Deccan Peasants' Uprising occurs in western India against high Ryotwari taxes and moneylenders.

title: Indian National Association Founded
event: The Indian National Association (Indian Association of Calcutta) is founded by Surendranath Banerjea and Ananda Mohan Bose.

title: Royal Titles Act, 1876
event: The Royal Titles Act of 1876 is passed, with Queen Victoria assuming the title of 'Kaiser-i-Hind' (Queen Empress of India).

title: ICS Age Limit Cut to 19
event: Under Viceroy Lytton, the maximum age limit for the Indian Civil Services (ICS) examination is reduced from 21 to 19 years.

title: Delhi Durbar, 1877
event: The grand Delhi Durbar is held by Lytton while the country is suffering under a severe famine.

title: Vernacular Press Act ('Gagging Act')
event: The repressive Vernacular Press Act (popularly called the 'Gagging Act') is enacted to muzzle the native press.

title: Indian Arms Act, 1878
event: The Indian Arms Act of 1878 is passed, criminalizing the possession of weapons by Indians without a license.

title: Statutory Civil Service Introduced
event: Lytton introduces the Statutory Civil Service, a short-lived system reserved for high-family nominations.

title: Pahariyas' Rebellion
event: The Pahariyas' Rebellion breaks out in the Raj Mahal Hills under Raja Jagganath against British expansion.

title: Ramosi Peasant Force Launched
event: The Ramosi Peasant Force is launched in Maharashtra by Vasudev Balwant Phadke.

title: Second Afghan War
event: The Second Afghan War (1878-80) intensifies under Lytton's Policy of 'Proud Reserve'.

title: Hicky's Bengal Gazette
event: Hicky's Bengal Gazette is established as the first printed newspaper in India.

title: First Indian Factory Act, 1881
event: The first Indian Factory Act is passed by Lord Ripon to improve working conditions for factory labourers.

title: Kesari & Maharatta Launched
event: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and others launch Kesari (Marathi daily) and Maharatta (English weekly).

title: Vernacular Press Act Repealed
event: Lord Ripon repeals the repressive Vernacular Press Act.

title: Anandamath Published
event: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee publishes Anandamath, popularizing the song 'Vandemataram' and the Sanyasi Revolt.

title: Hunter Education Commission
event: The Hunter Education Commission is appointed to review and improve primary and secondary education.

title: Indian National Conference
event: The first session of the Indian National Conference is held, serving as a precursor to the Congress.

title: Ilbert Bill Controversy
event: The Ilbert Bill controversy erupts as Ripon's government attempts to give Indian magistrates jurisdiction over Europeans.

title: Trial of Surendranath Banerjea
event: Trial of Surendranath Banerjea for contempt of court, marking a key moment in political press activism.

title: Madras Mahajan Sabha Founded
event: The Madras Mahajan Sabha is founded to coordinate provincial political activities.

title: Deccan Education Society Founded
event: The Deccan Education Society is founded in Pune by Ranade, Chiplunkar, and Agarkar.

title: Indian National Congress Founded
event: The Indian National Congress is founded by retired civil servant A.O. Hume, holding its first session in Bombay.

title: Bombay Presidency Association Founded
event: The Bombay Presidency Association is founded by Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang, and Badruddin Tyabji.

title: Third Burmese War
event: The Third Burmese War breaks out, leading to the complete annexation of Upper Burma.

title: Seva Sadan Established
event: The Seva Sadan is established in Bombay by Behramji Malabari to support women and children.

title: Dev Samaj Founded
event: The Dev Samaj is founded in Lahore by Shiv Narayan Agnihotri as a social and religious reform society.

title: Indian National Social Conference
event: The Indian National Social Conference is founded by M.G. Ranade and Raghunath Rao.

title: Dufferin's Attack on Congress
event: Viceroy Dufferin and colonial authorities launch a frontal attack on the newly formed Congress.

title: Ahmadiya Movement Founded
event: The Ahmadiya Movement is founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Qadian, Punjab.

title: Second Factory Act, 1891
event: The second Factory Act is passed, further regulating working hours and conditions.

title: Indian Councils Act, 1892
event: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 is enacted, expanding legislative council memberships and introducing indirect elections.

title: Madras Hindu Association Founded
event: The Madras Hindu Association is founded by Viresalingam Pantulu for social reform and education.

title: Durand Commission
event: The Durand Commission is set up under Lansdowne to define the boundary line between British India and Afghanistan.

title: Constitution of India Bill (Tilak)
event: The Constitution of India Bill (Home Rule Bill), inspired by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, is introduced to demand basic human rights.

title: Chapekar Brothers Assassinate Rand
event: The Chapekar brothers assassinate British officials Rand (the plague commissioner of Poona) and Lt. Ayerst in Maharashtra.

title: Ramakrishna Mission Founded
event: Swami Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission to carry out humanitarian and spiritual work.

title: Kaivartas' Movement Begins
event: The Kaivartas' (later Mahishyas) Movement begins in Midnapore, Bengal.

title: Mitra Mela Founded
event: The secret revolutionary society Mitra Mela is founded by Savarkar and his brother in Maharashtra.

title: Curzon Appointed Viceroy
event: Lord Curzon is appointed as Viceroy of India, initiating highly centralizing and reactionary policies.

title: Police Commission (Frazer)
event: Curzon appoints the Police Commission under Sir Andrew Frazer to review police administration.

title: Universities Commission
event: The Universities Commission is appointed by Curzon to recommend changes in university education.

title: Bharat Dharma Mahamandala Founded
event: The Bharat Dharma Mahamandala is established in Benaras by Madan Mohan Malaviya and others.

title: Anti-Partition Campaign Begins
event: The Anti-Partition Campaign is launched under Moderate leadership (Surendranath Banerjea, K.K. Mitra, etc.) in Bengal.

title: Indian Universities Act, 1904
event: The Indian Universities Act is passed, increasing government control over universities.

title: Ancient Monuments Preservation Act
event: The Ancient Monuments Preservation Act of 1904 is enacted by Curzon.

title: Mitra Mela Merges into Abhinav Bharat
event: The Mitra Mela secret society merges with Abhinav Bharat, modeled on Mazzini's 'Young Italy'.

title: Younghusband Mission to Lhasa
event: Colonel Younghusband leads a British military mission to Lhasa, Tibet.

title: Desher Katha Published
event: Desher Katha is published in Bengali by Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar, popularizing the economic critiques of Naoroji and Dutt.

title: Partition of Bengal
event: The Partition of Bengal is formally implemented by Curzon to divide the nationalist stronghold (October 16).

title: Swadeshi & Boycott Movement
event: The formal proclamation of the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement is made, urging self-reliance and national education.

title: Servants of India Society Founded
event: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founds the Servants of India Society to train national missionaries and workers.

title: Night School for Untouchables
event: Vitthal Ramji Shinde establishes a night school for the children of untouchables in Pune.

title: All India Muslim League Founded
event: The All India Muslim League is founded in Dacca by the Nawab of Dacca and the Aga Khan.

title: Congress Declares 'Swaraj' as Goal
event: The Calcutta Session of Congress, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, declares 'Swaraj' as the ultimate goal.

title: Depressed Classes Mission Founded
event: Shinde establishes the Depressed Classes Mission in Bombay to work for Dalit upliftment and eliminate untouchability.

title: Indian Millhands' Union Formed
event: Ashwini Coomar Banerjee leads jute mill workers to form the Indian Millhands' Union at Budge-Budge.

title: Yugantar, Sandhya & Kal Launched
event: Revolutionary nationalist journals Yugantar, Sandhya, and Kal are launched in Bengal and Maharashtra.

title: Surat Split
event: The Surat Split occurs as the Indian National Congress divides into Moderates and Extremists over techniques of struggle.

title: 'Home Political' Files Begun
event: The Reforms Office starts a new series of files, 'Home Political', to deal with political and communal issues.

title: Seditious Meetings Act, 1907
event: The Seditious Meetings Act is enacted to suppress anti-partition Swadeshi protests.

title: Alipore Conspiracy Case
event: Trial of Aurobindo Ghosh, Barindra Kumar Ghosh, and 36 others in the Alipore Conspiracy Case following bomb making raids.

title: Khudiram Bose's Muzaffarpur Bombing
event: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki assassinate two British women in a bomb attack meant for the Muzaffarpur Magistrate.

title: Barrah Dacoity
event: The Barrah dacoity is organized by Dacca Anushilan Samiti under Pulin Das to raise revolutionary funds.

title: Incitement & Explosives Acts, 1908
event: The Indian Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act and the Explosive Substances Act are passed to curb revolutionary activities.

title: Morley-Minto Reforms, 1909
event: The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909) are passed, introducing separate electorates for Muslims.

title: First Indian on Viceroy's Council
event: Satyendra Sinha is appointed as the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council.

title: Gandhi Writes Hind Swaraj
event: Mahatma Gandhi writes Hind Swaraj, outlining his political theory, critique of modern civilization, and concept of Swaraj.

title: Kanhere Assassinates Jackson
event: Anant Lakshman Kanhere, a member of Abhinav Bharat, assassinates Jackson, the Collector of Nasik.

title: Dhingra Assassinates Curzon-Wyllie
event: Madan Lal Dhingra assassinates Curzon-Wyllie in London; he is subsequently sentenced to death.

title: Poona Seva Sadan Founded
event: The Poona Seva Sadan is founded by Ramabai Ranade and G.K. Devadhar.

title: Punjab Hindu Sabha Founded
event: The Punjab Hindu Sabha is founded by U.N. Mukherji and Lal Chand.

title: Indian Press Act, 1910
event: The Indian Press Act of 1910 is enacted, imposing heavy security deposits on nationalist newspapers.

title: Bharat Stree Mahamandal Founded
event: Sarla Devi Chaudhurani establishes the Bharat Stree Mahamandal in Allahabad, the first major Indian women's organization.

title: Nishkam Karma Math Founded
event: Dhondo Keshav Karve establishes the Nishkam Karma Math (Monastery of Disinterested Work) in Pune.

title: Capital Shifts to Delhi
event: The Coronation Durbar of King George V is held in Delhi; the capital of India is officially transferred from Calcutta to Delhi.

title: Partition of Bengal Annulled
event: The Partition of Bengal is annulled in response to intense, sustained Swadeshi boycotts and protests.

title: Hitavada Begins Publication
event: The Hitavada starts publication in Nagpur to project the views of the Servants of India Society.

title: Social Service League Founded
event: The Social Service League is founded by N.M. Joshi in Bombay.

title: Ghadr Party Founded
event: The Ghadr Party is established in San Francisco by Lala Hardayal and other Indian immigrants to plot armed revolution.

title: Education Policy Resolution, 1913
event: The British Indian Government issues its Resolution on Education Policy, increasing grants for vernacular schools.

title: Bombay Chronicle Founded
event: The Bombay Chronicle daily newspaper is founded by Pherozeshah Mehta.

title: Outbreak of World War I
event: Outbreak of the First World War; Indian nationalists respond with varying levels of conditional support.

title: Gandhi Prepares to Leave South Africa
event: Mahatma Gandhi stays in South Africa until late in the year, preparing to return to India after concluding negotiations.

title: Seva Samiti Founded
event: The Seva Samiti is founded in Allahabad by Hridayanath Kunzru.

title: Ghadr Revolt Foiled
event: Ghadrite plans for a simultaneous armed revolt on February 21 in India are foiled due to treachery.

title: Hindu Mahasabha's First Session
event: The first session of the All India Hindu Mahasabha is held under the aegis of the Maharaja of Kasim Bazar.

title: Defence of India Act, 1915
event: The Defence of India Act is passed, giving the government sweeping powers of detention without trial.

title: Lucknow Pact
event: The Lucknow Session of Congress marks the reunion of Moderates and Extremists and the signing of the Lucknow Pact with the Muslim League.

title: Home Rule Leagues Launched
event: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant launch their respective Home Rule Leagues.

title: First Women's University (Poona)
event: The first Women's University is established at Poona by Dhondo Keshav Karve.

title: Champaran Satyagraha
event: Mahatma Gandhi launches the Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar, his first civil disobedience movement in India, fighting the indigo 'tin-kathia' system.

title: Montagu's 'Responsible Government' Declaration
event: Edwin Montagu, Secretary of State for India, makes his historic declaration in Parliament on 'responsible government' as the goal of British rule.

title: Sadler University Commission
event: The Sadler University Commission is appointed to recommend reforms in educational policy.

title: Indian Women's Association Founded
event: The Indian Women's Association is founded in Madras by Margaret Cousins and Annie Besant.

title: Ahmedabad Mill Strike
event: Gandhi leads the Ahmedabad Mill Strike, utilizing a hunger strike as a weapon of protest for the first time in India.

title: Kheda Satyagraha
event: Gandhi leads the Kheda Satyagraha (first non-cooperation) in Gujarat, advising farmers to withhold land revenue after crop failure.

title: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms Announced
event: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Montford Report) are announced, proposing a system of dyarchy in the provinces.

title: Rowlatt Act
event: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act (Rowlatt Act) is enacted, allowing trial without jury and deportation of suspects.

title: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
event: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre occurs in Amritsar (April 13) as Brigadier-General Dyer orders troops to fire on an unarmed crowd.

title: Government of India Act, 1919
event: The Government of India Act, 1919 is passed to implement the Montford Reforms, establishing dyarchy in provinces.

title: Evidence to Southborough Committee
event: Vitthal Ramji Shinde gives evidence before the Southborough Franchise Committee, demanding special representation for untouchables.

title: Non-Cooperation & Khilafat Movements
event: The Non-Cooperation and Khilafat Movements are launched jointly to protest against Punjab wrongs, the Treaty of Sevres, and demand Swaraj.

title: AITUC Founded
event: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) is founded to organize the growing Indian working class.

title: Hindustan Times Launched
event: The Hindustan Times daily newspaper is launched in Delhi.

title: Nagpur Session: New Congress Constitution
event: The Nagpur Congress Session adopts a new constitution for the Congress, aiming for Swaraj through peaceful means.

title: Death of Bal Gangadhar Tilak
event: Death of Bal Gangadhar Tilak on August 1, the day the Non-Cooperation Movement was launched.

title: Moplah Rebellion
event: The Moplah Rebellion breaks out in Malabar, Kerala, as a peasant uprising that later takes on communal overtones.

title: Buckingham & Carnatic Mills Strike
event: Labour strikes break out at the Buckingham and Carnatic textile mills in Madras under the leadership of Thiru Vika.

title: Chauri Chaura Incident
event: The Chauri Chaura incident (Feb 5) occurs as an agitated mob burns a police station; Gandhi withdraws the Non-Cooperation Movement.

title: Gaya Session Rejects Council Entry
event: The Gaya Session of Congress rejects the Swarajist proposal for entering legislative councils; C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru resign.

title: Gandhi's 'Great Trial' of 1922
event: Gandhi is arrested and sentenced to six years' imprisonment in the Great Trial of 1922.

title: Swarajya Party Formed
event: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru form the Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party (Swarajist Party) to contest elections and block councils from within.

title: Milap Urdu Daily Launched
event: The Milap Urdu daily newspaper is launched in Lahore.

title: Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case
event: The Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case begins, resulting in the imprisonment of communist leaders S.A. Dange and Muzaffar Ahmed.

title: Vaikom Satyagraha
event: The Vaikom Satyagraha is launched in Travancore, Kerala, demanding that temple roads be opened to untouchables.

title: Gandhi's Only Congress Presidency
event: Gandhi presides over his first and only Congress Session at Belgaum.

title: Ambedkar Launches Depressed Classes Movement
event: B.R. Ambedkar launches the Depressed Classes (Mahars) Movement to demand civil rights and equality.

title: Communist Party of India Founded
event: The Indian Communist Conference is held in Kanpur, formalizing the foundation of the Communist Party of India (CPI).

title: Kakori Train Robbery
event: The Kakori train robbery is executed by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) near Lucknow.

title: Indian Trade Union Act, 1926
event: The Indian Trade Union Act, 1926 is passed, providing legal recognition and registration to trade unions.

title: Kirti Journal Launched
event: The Kirti journal is launched in Punjab to propagate Marxist and socialist ideas.

title: Assassination of Swami Shraddhanand
event: Assassination of Swami Shraddhanand by a communal fanatic.

title: Simon Commission Appointed
event: The Simon Commission (Indian Statutory Commission) is appointed by the British Government with no Indian members.

title: All India Women's Conference Founded
event: The All India Women's Conference (AIWC) is established to promote women's education and socio-political status.

title: Harcourt Butler Indian States Commission
event: The Harcourt Butler Indian States Commission is appointed to study the relations between the Crown and princely states.

title: Ambedkar Starts Bahishkrit Bharat
event: B.R. Ambedkar starts the weekly journal Bahishkrit Bharat to advocate for the rights of the depressed classes.

title: 'Simon Go Back' Protests
event: The Simon Commission arrives in India, facing widespread black-flag protests and chants of 'Simon Go Back'.

title: Nehru Report
event: The Nehru Report is drafted by an all-parties committee headed by Motilal Nehru, outlining a constitution with Dominion Status.

title: Bardoli Satyagraha
event: The Bardoli Satyagraha is launched in Surat, Gujarat, against a 22 percent revenue hike, led successfully by Vallabhbhai Patel.

title: HRA Becomes HSRA
event: The HRA is reorganized into the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) under the leadership of Chandrashekhar Azad.

title: Assassination of Saunders
event: HSRA members Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev assassinate police officer Saunders to avenge Lala Lajpat Rai's death.

title: Lahore Session: 'Purna Swaraj' Adopted
event: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress, under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency, adopts 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) as its goal.

title: Meerut Conspiracy Case
event: Government arrests 31 prominent labour and communist leaders, launching the three-and-a-half-year Meerut Conspiracy Case trial.

title: Bhagat Singh's Assembly Bombing
event: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt throw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly to protest repressive bills.

title: Irwin's Dominion Status Declaration
event: Viceroy Lord Irwin issues a declaration stating that Dominion Status is the logical sequel to India's constitutional progress.

title: Hartog Committee Report
event: The Hartog Committee presents its report, highlighting a gloomy picture and high wastage in primary education.

title: Purna Swaraj Independence Pledge
event: The historic Purna Swaraj Independence Pledge is publicly taken all over India on January 26.

title: Gandhi's 11 Demands to Irwin
event: Gandhi presents his 11 Demands to Viceroy Lord Irwin, giving an ultimatum before starting mass struggle.

title: Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March)
event: Gandhi launches the Salt Satyagraha with the Dandi March (March 12 – April 6), initiating the Civil Disobedience Movement.

title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
event: The Chittagong Armoury Raid is carried out by Surya Sen and 65 activists under the Indian Republican Army banner.

title: First Round Table Conference
event: The First Round Table Conference meets in London; it is boycotted by the Congress.

title: Sarda Act (Child Marriage Restraint)
event: The Sarda Act (Child Marriage Restraint Act) is passed, raising the age of marriage.

title: Gandhi-Irwin Pact
event: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact is signed, suspending Civil Disobedience and allowing Congress participation in the next RTC.

title: Karachi Session: Fundamental Rights Resolution
event: The Karachi Session of Congress endorses the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and passes a resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Programme.

title: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru & Sukhdev Hanged
event: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev are hanged on March 23 in Lahore jail.

title: Second Round Table Conference
event: The Second Round Table Conference is held in London; Gandhi attends as the sole representative of the Congress.

title: Communal Award
event: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announces the Communal Award, granting separate electorates to depressed classes.

title: Poona Pact
event: Gandhi goes on a fast unto death in Yeravada jail, ending with the Poona Pact which grants reserved seats instead of separate electorates.

title: Third Round Table Conference
event: The Third Round Table Conference is held in London, boycotted by the Congress.

title: NWFP Made a Governor's Province
event: The North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) is constituted as a governor's province.

title: Individual Civil Disobedience Resumes
event: Resumption of the Civil Disobedience Movement in the form of Individual Civil Disobedience.

title: India Peasants' Institute Founded
event: N.G. Ranga establishes the India Peasants' Institute to train peasant activists.

title: Civil Disobedience Movement Withdrawn
event: The Civil Disobedience Movement is formally withdrawn by the Congress.

title: Congress Socialist Party Formed
event: The Congress Socialist Party (CSP) is formed within the Congress by Acharya Narendra Dev and Jayaprakash Narayan.

title: Government of India Act, 1935
event: The Government of India Act, 1935 is passed, proposing provincial autonomy, dyarchy at the centre, and an all-India federation.

title: Burma Separated from India
event: Burma is officially separated from British India under the provisions of the 1935 Act.

title: All India Kisan Sabha Founded
event: The All India Kisan Sabha (Kisan Congress) is established in Lucknow, with Sahjanand Saraswati as President.

title: Bakasht Movement Begins
event: The Bakasht Movement begins in Bihar under the Kisan Sabha against landlord occupancy policies.

title: Provincial Elections; Congress Wins
event: General elections are held for provincial assemblies; Congress wins a majority and forms ministries in eight provinces.

title: Wardha Scheme (Nai Talim)
event: The Zakir Hussain Committee formulates the Wardha Scheme of Basic Education (Nai Talim) based on Gandhian principles.

title: Haripura Session (Bose Presides)
event: The Haripura Session of the Congress is held under the presidency of Subhas Chandra Bose.

title: National Planning Committee Formed
event: The Congress establishes the National Planning Committee, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, to draft industrialization plans.

title: Outbreak of World War II
event: Outbreak of World War II; the Viceroy associates India in the war without consulting Indian representatives.

title: Congress Ministries Resign
event: All provincial Congress ministries resign in protest against India's unilateral involvement in World War II.

title: Tripuri Session; Bose Forms Forward Bloc
event: The Tripuri Session of Congress is held; Subhas Bose resigns as President due to ideological conflicts with Gandhi and forms the Forward Bloc.

title: Muslim League's Lahore Resolution
event: The Muslim League passes its Lahore Resolution demanding independent, sovereign states in Muslim-majority regions.

title: The 'August Offer'
event: Viceroy Linlithgow announces the 'August Offer', promising a representative constituent assembly and dominion status after the war.

title: Individual Satyagraha Launched
event: The Congress launches Individual Satyagraha to assert freedom of speech, with Vinoba Bhave as the first satyagrahi.

title: Anti-Compromise Conference (Ramgarh)
event: Subhas Bose convenes the Anti-Compromise Conference at Ramgarh to oppose imperialist war contributions.

title: Subhas Bose's Great Escape
event: Subhas Chandra Bose escapes from surveillance at his house in Calcutta to mobilize armed support from abroad.

title: Cripps Mission
event: The Cripps Mission arrives in India; its draft proposals are rejected by the Congress and Muslim League.

title: 'Quit India' Resolution
event: The All India Congress Committee passes the 'Quit India' Resolution (August 8); all prominent leaders are arrested the next morning.

title: INA's First Phase (Mohan Singh)
event: Captain Mohan Singh establishes the first phase of the Indian National Army (INA) in Singapore with Japanese support.

title: Parallel Governments Formed
event: Parallel governments are formed in Ballia (UP), Tamluk (Bengal), and Satara (Maharashtra) during the Quit India upsurge.

title: Bengal Famine
event: A devastating famine strikes Bengal, causing severe loss of life.

title: Gandhi's 21-Day Prison Fast
event: Mahatma Gandhi undergoes a 21-day fast in prison (February) against state repression of the Quit India movement.

title: Bose Takes Command of the INA
event: Subhas Chandra Bose arrives in Singapore and takes over control of the Indian Independence League and the INA.

title: C.R. Formula
event: C. Rajagopalachari publishes the CR Formula to resolve the constitutional deadlock on the basis of a post-war plebiscite.

title: Desai-Liaqat Pact Proposals
event: The Desai-Liaqat Pact proposals are discussed, proposing equal representation for Congress and League in the executive.

title: Wavell Plan & Shimla Conference
event: Viceroy Lord Wavell announces the Wavell Plan and convenes the Shimla Conference; talks break down over League veto claims.

title: End of World War II
event: End of the Second World War as Japan surrenders.

title: INA Trials Begin (Red Fort)
event: The first public trial of INA officers (Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal, Gurbaksh Dhillon) opens in the Red Fort, New Delhi.

title: Congress Backs the INA Prisoners
event: The first post-war Congress session is held in Bombay, declaring absolute support for the INA prisoners' cause.

title: Royal Indian Navy (RIN) Mutiny
event: Over 1,100 Royal Indian Navy (RIN) ratings go on strike on HMIS Talwar, triggering a massive, supportive working-class strike wave.

title: Cabinet Mission
event: The Cabinet Mission arrives in New Delhi and recommends the Cabinet Mission Plan, proposing a three-tier federal structure.

title: Direct Action Day
event: The Muslim League calls for 'Direct Action Day' (August 16) to achieve Pakistan, leading to the Calcutta Killings and communal riots.

title: Interim Government Sworn In
event: The Interim Government, headed by Jawaharlal Nehru as Vice President of the Executive Council, is sworn in.

title: Telangana Peasant Insurrection
event: The armed Telangana Peasant Insurrection is launched in Nalgonda, Hyderabad state, against oppressive deshmukhs.

title: Constituent Assembly's First Meeting
event: The Constituent Assembly of India holds its historic first meeting to frame a constitution (December 9).

title: Attlee's Transfer-of-Power Deadline
event: British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announces a deadline of June 30, 1948, for the transfer of power and British departure from India.

title: Mountbatten Sworn In as Viceroy
event: Lord Mountbatten is sworn in as the last Viceroy of British India to oversee the transfer of power.

title: Mountbatten Plan (June 3 Plan)
event: The Mountbatten Plan (June 3 Plan) is announced, proposing immediate partition and transfer of power on dominion status basis.

title: Indian Independence Act, 1947
event: The British Parliament passes the Indian Independence Act of 1947, receiving royal assent on July 18.

title: Radcliffe Boundary Commissions
event: The boundary commissions under Sir Cyril Radcliffe are appointed to partition Punjab and Bengal.

title: Creation of Pakistan
event: Creation of the independent dominion of Pakistan on August 14.

title: Indian Independence
event: Creation of the independent dominion of India on August 15, ending nearly two centuries of British rule.

title: Princely States Begin Acceding
event: Under Sardar Patel, the first phase of princely states' integration is completed as 136 states sign Instruments of Accession.
